text: We will send packets to this physical layer. We will go up in the IP layer, and then through other routers that are in the internet. So this is how networks work. Okay, we are going to focus on Wi-Fi in our case, so only on this wireless connectivity between the user device and the access point. But it is important that you understand what is behind the Wi-Fi access point. Behind the Wi-Fi access point, there are routers. Routers are network nodes where we find the physical layer, the MAC layer, another layer that it doesn't matter right now, and the IP layer. And routers are able to route packets toward the internet. Okay, so packets will hop from one router to another, till we reach the router that is the first router that is in the internet. That is called gateway today. And then once you are there, you are in the internet. Okay, and there are other routers that route your packet depending on where the packet has to go. Similarly, when we want to receive information, let's say.
